text: North Richmond Street. <break time="0.8s" /> Being a dead end. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a quiet street. <break time="0.8s" /> Except at the hour. <break time="0.8s" /> When the Christian Brothers School. <break time="0.8s" /> Set the boys free. <break time="0.8s" /> At the blind end. <break time="0.8s" /> Stood an uninhabited house. <break time="0.8s" /> Of two storeys. <break time="0.8s" /> Detached from its neighbours. <break time="0.8s" /> On a square ground. <break time="0.8s" /> The other houses of the street. <break time="0.8s" /> Conscious of decent lives within them. <break time="0.8s" /> Gazed at one another. <break time="0.8s" /> With brown, imperturbable faces. <break time="0.8s" /> The former tenant of our house. <break time="0.8s" /> A priest. <break time="0.8s" /> Had died in the back drawing room. <break time="0.8s" /> And the air. <break time="0.8s" /> Musty from having been long enclosed. <break time="0.8s" /> Hung in all the rooms. <break time="0.8s" /> Among the useless papers. <break time="0.8s" /> In the waste room behind the kitchen. <break time="0.8s" /> I found a few old books. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose pages were curled and damp. <break time="0.8s" /> He had been a very charitable priest. <break time="0.8s" /> For in his will he had left all his money. <break time="0.8s" /> To institutions. <break time="0.8s" /> And the furniture of his house. <break time="0.8s" /> To his sister. <break time="0.8s" /> When the short days of winter came. <break time="0.8s" /> Dusk fell. <break time="0.8s" /> Before we had well eaten our dinners. <break time="0.8s" /> And we played. <break time="0.8s" /> In the dark, muddy lanes. <break time="0.8s" /> Behind the houses. <break time="0.8s" /> If Mangans sister came out. <break time="0.8s" /> On the doorstep to call her brother in to his tea. <break time="0.8s" /> We watched her. <break time="0.8s" /> From our shadow. <break time="0.8s" /> Peering up and down the street.
